title: Express: routes, middleware and error handling

videos.script:
In the last lesson you wrote a link shortener with nothing installed. {{plumbing}} Most of its hundred lines were not about links. They routed requests, wrote replies, read bodies, and caught errors. Today Express does that work, and you keep only the part that is yours.

{{routes}} First, routes and routers, and the order Express tries them in. Then the pattern language of Express five, which is smaller than the old one on purpose. A tutorial from version four will fail at start-up, and you will see why that is a feature.

{{chain}} Then middleware, the idea everything in Express is built from. A chain of functions, each one answering or passing the request on. You will write a logger, and a check for an admin key. And you will forget to pass a request on, and watch it hang.

{{errors}} Then errors. Express five catches an error from an async route, which version four did not. And its default error page shows your stack trace to anybody, unless one variable says production.

{{app}} Last, the links service again, in five small files, with tests that start it on a port of their own.
